matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: When the numeric discrepancy is a multiple of 1, try moving a single vertical stick (the I) from one numeral to another, turning the source numeral into a lower‑value symbol (e.g., II→I) and the target into a higher‑value symbol (e.g., I→II).
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation is off by ±1, ±2, ±3, or ±4 and a vertical stick can be transferred without breaking either numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing a vertical stick from a numeral that becomes empty (e.g., turning I into nothing) or leaving the source numeral invalid.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First attempt to fix the equation by moving a stick within the same character; common intra‑character changes include turning X into V (or V into X) by repositioning a diagonal stick, or converting L into I by removing a horizontal, etc.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is close to correct and a single‑character transformation could adjust the value by 5, 10, or 50.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and discarding it, leaving a single diagonal stick (invalid).

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, check that every resulting character is a recognized Roman numeral or allowed operator; any stray diagonal or isolated vertical that does not match a symbol invalidates the solution.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before arithmetic verification.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal stick after taking one from X, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; when moving a diagonal from X or V, ensure the remaining shape stays a valid numeral (e.g., X→V) rather than leaving a lone diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick is removed from a character that originally contained diagonals.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from X and not repositioning it, resulting in a single diagonal.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign, which is a valid operator. The removed vertical stick can then be used elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation needs a subtraction instead of addition, or if a vertical stick is needed for another numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' and discarding it, leaving a stray stick.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new valid Roman numeral (e.g., moving a vertical stick to create an extra I) provided the source character remains valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a small amount and there is a spare stick that can become a new numeral without breaking the source.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I and leaving the source empty, which is not allowed.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If intra‑character moves fail, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character, ensuring both source and destination remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character options and the equation is still incorrect.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from '+' to an I but forgetting to change '+' to '-' (leaving an invalid operator).

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: After converting '+' to '-', the freed vertical stick can be attached to a nearby numeral to increase its value (e.g., turning I into II).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a subtraction operator is needed and a numeral could benefit from an extra vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' but not attaching it to any numeral, leaving the stick unused.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of the left‑hand side and right‑hand side after any transformation; the equality must hold in standard Roman‑numeral arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After a candidate transformation passes symbol validation.
matchstick.example: Accepting a visually valid equation that actually computes 12 = 13 + 4, which is false.

matchstick.title: Do not modify the equals sign
matchstick.principle: The equals sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; moving a stick from it either destroys the operator or creates a different operator, and you cannot recreate a proper '=' elsewhere with a single stick. Therefore, keep the '=' unchanged.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving; treat the '=' as immutable unless you can simultaneously create a new '=' elsewhere, which is impossible with a single stick.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal from '=' to turn it into '-' and not forming a new '=' elsewhere, resulting in an equation with no equals sign.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to consider moving sticks between characters first, missing simpler intra‑character changes that can fix the equation with a single modification.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Systematically check each character for possible single‑stick transformations (X→V, V→X, L→I, etc.) before exploring inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a diagonal stick without ensuring the remaining shape stays a valid numeral, creating an isolated diagonal that doesn't correspond to any Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When removing a diagonal from a character, immediately decide how to reposition it so that the source character stays valid (e.g., turn X into V) or avoid removing it altogether.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on visual validity of symbols but forgets to verify that the numeric equality holds.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any valid symbol transformation, compute the numeric values of both sides and confirm the equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes the equals sign or other operators without checking that the equation still contains exactly one equals sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat the equals sign as immutable; if you modify it, you must simultaneously create a new equals sign elsewhere, which is impossible with a single stick, so avoid modifying it.

matchstick.description: Forgetting to place the removed stick after modifying an operator (e.g., converting plus to minus) and leaving it unused
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from an operator but doesn't reuse it, violating the rule that the stick must be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After converting '+' to '-', immediately attach the freed vertical stick to a numeral or use it to form a new valid character.
